affectedPublicSurfaces: demo.app-juli.com replay path — Decisions list, review page (/decisions/recommendations/<key>), staged run route (apps/demo)

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Load the candidate demo build — zero public canary traffic. The change removes a request from the replay path rather than adding one
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: Issue's own Release evidence section, transcribed verbatim. The defect is that the replay path issues GET /v1/demo/analytics via ImpactBlock mounted by the review page, violating ADR-094 decision 1.

journeys.name: replay-walk-issues-no-authenticated-request
assertions: Dùng thử Demo → Decisions → approve → review page → staged run view → confirm
the browser issues NO /v1/* request at any point in that walk — including GET /v1/demo/analytics from the review page
no Supabase session is created and no bearer token is stored

journeys.name: signed-in-surfaces-still-load-analytics
assertions: the analytics screen still loads its data — the fix must not disable analytics where it is legitimately wanted
a signed-in review page still renders its impact figures rather than an empty state caused by this fix

staticAssetChecks.notes: No new assets. The captured scenario must still be present in the built artifact — verify-replay-scenario-in-build.mjs stays wired and passing.

migrationCompatibility.notes: Issue text: 'No migration.' Client-side fetch suppression and a widened structural test in apps/demo.

rollbackAssertion.notes: Issue text: a rollback must not silently restore the analytics call on the replay path. The pre-change behaviour is the LESS correct one, so a rollback is a recorded regression rather than a neutral revert.

doNotInfer: release evidence fields beyond what the issue's Release evidence (ADR-035) section states
disabling analytics anywhere it is legitimately wanted — the /analytics screen and the signed-in review page must keep working
suppressing the request by unmounting or hiding ImpactBlock on surfaces where the seller should see impact figures
narrowing #1319's exclusion note instead of removing it — the claim that the analytics fetch is reached only by an explicit visit to /analytics is false
hand-maintaining the module-graph test's entry points when they could be derived from the routes the replay journey visits
weakening the exit-gate journey's zero-/v1/* assertion to make it pass
